title: How he met Sue, their life together and her death
summary: He met Sue, a chorus dancer, at Robinson's Restaurant, lived with her twenty years, learned only after her death of the family epilepsy.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You were telling me about taking your
wife to Seidenham. You want to go back and tell me how you met her?

See, I used to play around at the theater, see. And she was a dancing girl in the chorus. And I was at Robinson's Restaurant. And I was playing the piano and this girl come in, she had a blue gown on, blue dress on. And came over and put her arms around me. I says, "take your arms from around me, your husband will --" and she said, "I'm not married." I says, "no?" I says, "What's your telephone number?" So she give it to me.

So I call her up the next day and a man answered. I said, ah, you can't trust these women. So the next time I saw her it was about a week later. And I'm walking down in front of the theater and I saw her, and I says, "hey, there." I says, "I thought you said you wasn't married." She says, "well, that's my brother, he answered the phone."
So, Ralph Cooper used to say, "Where's Sue?"
Ralph Cooper was the entertainer at the --
Yeah, Ralph Cooper used to say, "Where's Sue?" I'd say, "Sue's around here somewhere." So kept on -- I
liked her and we got to going together and I said, let's get married. But I didn't get married, but I got an apartment and we lived together.

And we lived together 20 years, and I used to go on the road and call her up and say, 'hey, get on the train, there's somebody here that wants to see you. So get on a plane and fly in.' We used to go to Chicago, meet all the girls and everything. And I didn't know she was an epileptic until after she died. Because her doctor didn't tell me that, see.
How did you find out, Tom?

The doctor -- I asked the doctor, what's the matter with her? He couldn't cure her. He said, she's an epileptic. I said, what's that? He said, I don't know. Everyone in the family was an epileptic. Her sister went in a coma and her brother, same way. They all were epileptic, and went in coma and never came out of it.

So I was in -- I think I was in Chicago and she was in the hospital and they called me up and says, you'd better come back as soon as you can because I don't think she's going to live. And I came in early in the morning, and I think it was Sunday morning. The sun was rising when I left the hospital, and she died right after that.
A lovely wife, what was her name?
Sue, beautiful soul, all of them.
